findings.comment:
Several pans of potentially hazardous food (PHF) in the bottom of the prep cooler were undated as to when they were prepared and were not used within 24 hours of preparation.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
The pans of food were dated to CORRECT the violation.  None had been prepared more than 2 days ago.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
(A) Soup in a crock pot on the counter in the waitress station was 125 degrees.      (B) Food in the top warming drawer under the order counter was 119 degrees.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)
The temperature in the crock pot and the drawer were both increased to maintain a hot holding temperature of 135 degrees or more to CORRECT the violation.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Raw bacon was stored over cheese and produce in the black refrigerator in the back storage room.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.
The bacon was put in another cooler below any pre-cooked and ready-to-eat food to CORRECT the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:  (A) cart to the left of the fryers,   (B) top of stove around the burners.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean the above-referenced surfaces.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The bathroom door in the back storage room is not self-closing.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.
A self-closing mechanism has been purchased.  Put it on the door.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Two sides of  the bathroom in the back storage room has no coving or baseboard on the wall-to-floor junction.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
Placing coving or baseboard on the wall-to-floor junction.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Paint or tile material is chipping in the ceiling above the order counter on the kitchen side.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.
Remove the chipping material and paint the places that are chipped.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Tongs and spatulas that were used to handle food were stored at room temperature.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
The utensils were stored on the grill which was very hot to correct the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Towels were used to line shelves where wet utensils were placed after washing.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
The towels were removed.  Clean and sanitize the shelves regularly rather than use clean towels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The large and small upright freezers were in need of defrosting.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Defrost the freezers.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
The plates on the wire shelf above the order counter were stored food side up.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.
Store the plates inverted or covered.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(A) There is a hole in the wall caused by the door knob in the men's restroom.
(B) There is hole in the wall by the stool in the women's restroom.
(C) The ceiling tiles in both restrooms are rough.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning.  
Repair and paint the damaged walls.  On or before the next remodel of the bathrooms, replace the tiles with ones that are smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
A spray bottle of cleaner was unlabeled as to its contents.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
The bottle was labeled.
